doc.title: Ellis Marsalis — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Jazz Room with Blackwell and the Playboy Club
summary: He plays the Jazz Room, then the Playboy Club backing Black artists until they stopped coming.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Who were you working with when you came back to New Orleans? You were saying jobs were scarce.
I had a gig with Blackwell for a while. Blackwell had a gig in a place called the Jazz Room in the French Quarter. It’s basically Otis Duvernay.
So he – I’m sorry. Blackwell had gone with you in, I guess, ’56, or you had gone with Blackwell to hook up with Ornette. So now he’s back in New Orleans . . .
. . . instead of having continued his career with . . . .
Do you know what precipitated his leaving Ornette or returning back to New Orleans?

No. I don’t know. I was playing at this club for a while. Eventually Edward was able to get Nat Perrilliat on the gig. So it was really a quartet. But me and the owner got into it, and that was it. I was gone.

The Jazz Room, where Ed Blackwell was working. I’m trying to think. That was before I started playing at the Playboy Club, but eventually I did start playing at the Playboy Club. When I started – at that time we were hired to play behind all the black artists that the Playboy Club had signed. Ironically, the club in New Orleans was the second club that they built. It was even built before the one in New York. So we must
have stayed on that gig for about two or three months. Eventually the black artists stopped coming, and we didn’t have a gig no more. That was it.
On – let me see – on Iberville, I think. Right off the corner of Bourbon – I think Bourbon and Iberville.
